Life-like Automaton With Definable Rules

AlgorithmsLogicCounting
Game: Decide which neighbour counts create life and which let it continue.
How to play: Click cells to draw, tick the B and S boxes (or pick a preset), then step or run.

Look for the math

Changing two short lists of numbers creates entirely different universes.

Birth and survival sets

A rule is written B…/S…: an empty cell is born when its neighbour count is in B, and a live cell survives when its count is in S. Conway's Life is B3/S23. The page's example B135/S35 gives a different world from B3/S23 with the same starting pattern.

A family of automata

HighLife (B36/S23) adds a self-replicating pattern; Seeds (B2/S) has no survival at all, so nothing persists from one generation to the next; Life without Death (B3/S012345678) can only grow. The logic test checks these rules, Conway's blinker, rule toggling and the reverse step.

Start from Conway, then add 6 to the birth set. What new pattern appears?
